data.title: Metric — kadence
body: # Metric — kadence
> **Superseded 2026-09-16 by [strategy.md](DOC-35).** Kept as history; where the two disagree, strategy.md wins.

- **Method caveat:** the North Star skill explicitly does not recommend defining an NSM in the early discovery phase — while it is still unknown what value the product delivers. Formally, that is exactly where we are. So what follows is a **validation-phase metric**, and a full NSM tree only makes sense after the first users.
## Why not stars

GitHub stars are the classic vanity metric: they measure how many people found the idea interesting, not how many use it. A project can have 3000 stars and zero live repositories. For us this is especially dangerous, because the idea sounds attractive and will collect stars even if nobody needs the product — that is, the metric will show success exactly when we are failing.
## The metric
> **The number of repositories whose event journal has entries from at least two different authors 14 days after `kadence init`.**
Every condition here is deliberate:
| Condition | Why |
| **repositories**, not users | the unit of value is a team, not an installation |
| **two different authors** | the only proof that the tool survived team use, where conflicts are possible at all |
| **14 days** | long enough to outlast curiosity, and short enough to measure quickly |
| **entries in the journal**, not a CLI launch | an event means work, not installation |
## Input metrics
1. `init` per week — the top of the funnel
2. The share who reach the 10th event — crossing the "tried it and dropped it" threshold
3. The share of repositories with a second author — team use
4. The share with at least one closed sprint — whether they reach velocity, our differentiator
## Leading signals
- Issues asking "how do I do X" — a sign of real use, not a passing look
- Forks with edits of their own
- Mentions in other people's `AGENTS.md`
## Counter-metrics
| Metric | Threshold | Why |
| Command time | ≤ 200 ms | Guardrail from [ADR-005](DOC-8) |
| Size of `.kadence/` | ≤ 5 MB per 10k events | Repository bloat is a solid reason to delete it |
| Conflicts in the journal | **0** | One defeat here kills the product's whole thesis |
| Share of `init` with no second event | < 50% | If most drop out immediately, the problem is in the first experience |
## The measurement problem that has to be named
**We will not be able to measure this.** The product is offline, there is no telemetry and there never will be — that is a principle from [SPEC.md](../../SPEC.md), the "Never" section.

So the metric is honest in substance but unobservable. The real sources at the start: public repositories with a `.kadence/` directory via GitHub search, answers in issues, directly surveying the first users.

This is a limitation, not a flaw in the wording: user privacy matters more than our convenience in measuring. But planning has to proceed knowing that feedback will be rare and biased toward public repositories.
